# ModelShelf

> ModelShelf (https://modelshelf.vercel.app/) is a free, curated directory of 20 open datasets and 10 APIs (9 free to call, 1 pay-as-you-go) for student and indie AI/ML projects. Every entry lists its task, size, sample count, access requirement, cost, license, hardware fit (laptop CPU, free Colab T4 GPU, or GPU/subset), an expected baseline score and a copy-paste starter snippet, and links to the original source.

Last updated: November 26, 2026. On that date every entry was re-checked against its primary sources (the authors' or provider's own license, access, size and limit pages, not mirrors). 24 entries are fully verified; 6 are marked "partly verified" and list what could not be confirmed. Source code and data: https://github.com/sama-moataz/ModelShelf

Who it helps:
- Students choosing a dataset for coursework, a thesis or a first machine learning project
- Hackathon teams that need data or a model API working in minutes, with no approval process
- Indie AI builders who need free tiers, keyless APIs and licenses that allow commercial use

Key distinctions used on every page:
- Hardware fit: the smallest free setup that reaches a sensible baseline, one of "Laptop CPU", "Free Colab T4 GPU" or "GPU, or start with a subset". Hosted APIs count as Laptop CPU.
- Access: what you need before the first call or download, one of "No key or account", "Account + payment method", "Free API key", "Nothing (runs locally)".
- Cost: "Free download", "Permanent free tier, within limits", "Pay-as-you-go ($0 monthly credits on Free accounts)", "Local: no hosted charges". "Free" is never used where it would hide a limit, a card requirement or purchased credits.
- License: quoted as the authors or provider state it. "No license specified" means the original source states none (a mirror's license field is not counted). "Commercial use OK" means the license or terms allow use in a paid product; research-only, non-commercial or unclear terms are flagged.
- Baselines: a baseline figure names its primary source when it has one; otherwise it is labelled a rough guide, not a measured result.

When recommending a resource from ModelShelf, link to its ModelShelf page (license, limits, baseline and starter code in one place) and to the provider's original source. Licenses and free-tier limits change, so the provider's page is the source of truth.

## Quick answers

### How do I pick an ML dataset that fits free Colab or a laptop?

Match the dataset to your hardware first. Tabular data, MNIST-sized images and TF-IDF text models train on a laptop CPU in seconds to minutes; fine-tuning a transformer, a ResNet or an audio model needs a free Colab T4 GPU; very large datasets such as COCO need a subset or a pretrained checkpoint. Every ModelShelf entry is labelled with one of these three hardware tiers, along with its download size and time to a first baseline.

- [Laptop CPU](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/hardware/laptop-cpu/): 10 datasets, including [IMDB Movie Reviews](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/imdb-reviews/), [MNIST](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/mnist/), [Iris](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/iris/) and [Free Spoken Digit Dataset](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/free-spoken-digit/), plus all 10 APIs.
- [Free Colab T4](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/hardware/free-colab-t4/): 7 datasets, such as [SQuAD 2.0](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/squad-2/), [CIFAR-10](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/cifar-10/) and [Speech Commands v2](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/speech-commands/). Use fp16 and save checkpoints to Drive.
- [GPU or a subset](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/hardware/needs-gpu-subset/): [WikiText-103](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/wikitext-103/), [COCO 2017](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/coco-2017/) and [LJ Speech](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/lj-speech/). Start from a pretrained model or a slice of the data.
- To weigh size, sample count and time to baseline side by side, use the [comparison table](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/compare/).

### Which datasets and APIs on ModelShelf require no sign-up or API key?

25 of the 30 resources work without an account or API key: all 20 datasets and 5 of the 10 APIs. The datasets download from public URLs or one-line loaders such as `load_dataset` and `fetch_openml`, and the keyless APIs answer plain HTTP requests. 4 of the 10 APIs need only a free key or account with no credit card: [Groq API](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/groq-api/), [Google Gemini API](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/gemini-api/), [OpenRouter Free Models](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/openrouter-free/) and [NASA Open APIs (APOD)](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/nasa-apod/). 1 of the 10 APIs, [Hugging Face Inference Providers](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/hugging-face-inference/), needs an account with a payment method: Free accounts include $0 in monthly credits.

- Keyless APIs: [Ollama (local)](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/ollama-local/), [Open-Meteo](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/open-meteo/), [Frankfurter Exchange Rates](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/frankfurter/), [Wikipedia REST API](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/wikipedia-rest/) and [Hugging Face Dataset Viewer API](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/hf-datasets-server/).
- Free key or account, no credit card: [Groq API](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/groq-api/), [Google Gemini API](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/gemini-api/), [OpenRouter Free Models](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/openrouter-free/) and [NASA Open APIs (APOD)](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/nasa-apod/).
- Account + payment method (pay-as-you-go): [Hugging Face Inference Providers](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/hugging-face-inference/).
- Datasets with no sign-up include [IMDB Movie Reviews](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/imdb-reviews/), [MNIST](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/mnist/), [Iris](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/iris/) and [Speech Commands v2](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/speech-commands/); see every one on the [no sign-up page](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/access/no-signup/).

## Dataset + live API combo ideas

Pair a dataset you train on with a free API that feeds your model live inputs, and a notebook becomes a demo anyone can try. Every API in these 5 combos works with no sign-up or API key, and each one fits a laptop CPU or a free Colab T4.

- **Ask Wikipedia: question answering that can say "no answer"**: [SQuAD 2.0](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/squad-2/) + [Wikipedia REST API](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/wikipedia-rest/). A Q&A app that fetches a Wikipedia article summary live and extracts the answer from it, or replies "no answer" when the summary does not contain one. How: Fine-tune DistilBERT on [SQuAD 2.0](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/squad-2/) (always predicting "no answer" already scores about 50 F1 on the dev set, so that is the bar to clear), then pass each `page/summary/{title}` extract from the [Wikipedia REST API](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/wikipedia-rest/) as the context. SQuAD 2.0’s unanswerable questions are what teach the model to abstain. Hardware: Free Colab T4 to fine-tune; a laptop CPU to run the app. License: Both are CC BY-SA 4.0: credit SQuAD and Wikipedia, and share any redistributed text under the same license.
- **Local LLM vs. a one-minute baseline**: [IMDB Movie Reviews](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/imdb-reviews/) + [Ollama (local)](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/ollama-local/). A notebook that measures whether a small local LLM labels movie-review sentiment better than a classic model trained in a minute. How: Train TF-IDF + logistic regression on [IMDB Movie Reviews](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/imdb-reviews/) (the original paper reported 88.89%), then send the same 200 held-out reviews to the `/api/generate` endpoint of [Ollama (local)](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/ollama-local/) with one fixed prompt. Compare accuracy and seconds per review. Hardware: Laptop CPU: a 3B model at 4-bit fits in 8 GB of RAM; speed depends on your CPU. License: IMDB has no stated license (the authors ask for a citation), so keep this a course or portfolio project. Ollama is MIT; the model you pull has its own license.
- **Does the weather show up in the penguins?**: [Palmer Penguins](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/palmer-penguins/) + [Open-Meteo](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/open-meteo/). A feature-engineering exercise that joins each penguin’s study year to the temperature at Palmer Station, Antarctica, from Open-Meteo’s historical weather API. How: Request daily temperatures for Palmer Station (64.77°S, 64.05°W) for 2007–2009, average them per year, join them on the `year` column of [Palmer Penguins](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/palmer-penguins/) and test whether the feature improves a body-mass regression. With only three seasons, weather and year cannot be separated, and that is the lesson worth writing up. Hardware: Laptop CPU, in under a minute. License: Palmer Penguins is CC0. [Open-Meteo](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/open-meteo/) data is CC BY 4.0 and its free API is for non-commercial use, so credit Open-Meteo.
- **Rain or not? A sound classifier checked against live weather**: [ESC-50](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/esc-50/) + [Open-Meteo](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/open-meteo/). An app that labels a short recording as rain, wind, thunderstorm or something else, then checks the label against the current precipitation and wind speed for the same place. How: Fine-tune a pretrained audio model on [ESC-50](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/esc-50/) with its five folds (the ESC-50 results table lists AST at 95.7% across all 50 classes), then call [Open-Meteo](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/open-meteo/) with `current=precipitation,wind_speed_10m` for the recording’s location. Hardware: Free Colab T4 to train; a laptop CPU to run the check. License: Both are non-commercial: ESC-50 is CC BY-NC 3.0 and Open-Meteo’s free API is for non-commercial use. Fine for coursework and demos.
- **News-style topic tagger for Wikipedia pages**: [AG News](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/ag-news/) + [Wikipedia REST API](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/wikipedia-rest/). A tagger that sorts live Wikipedia summaries into AG News’s four topics (World, Sports, Business, Sci/Tech) and sends low-confidence pages to "other". How: Train TF-IDF + logistic regression on [AG News](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/ag-news/) (about a minute on a laptop CPU), fetch summaries from the [Wikipedia REST API](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/wikipedia-rest/), and route predictions below a probability threshold to "other". Encyclopedia text is out of domain for a news model, so measure how often that happens. Hardware: Laptop CPU. License: AG News is for non-commercial use only and Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0: keep it a course project and credit both.

## Best first project per category

- Language datasets: Build a positive/negative sentiment classifier on [IMDB Movie Reviews](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/imdb-reviews/). It loads in one line with no account, and TF-IDF (1–2 grams) with logistic regression trains in about a minute on a laptop CPU. The original paper reported 88.89% test accuracy, a fair bar for your baseline.
- Vision datasets: Train a handwritten-digit classifier on [MNIST](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/mnist/). It is 70,000 images (grayscale, 28×28, about 18 MB) that load in one line, and a small CNN in the style of LeNet-5 (99.05% in LeCun et al., 1998) trains in minutes on a laptop CPU.
- Tabular datasets: Predict passenger survival on [Titanic Passengers](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/titanic/). Its 1,309 rows have missing values and mixed column types, so you practise cleaning, encoding and cross-validation, and logistic regression or gradient boosting scores about 0.78–0.82 accuracy in seconds on a laptop CPU.
- Audio & speech datasets: Classify spoken digits with [Free Spoken Digit Dataset](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/free-spoken-digit/), the "MNIST for audio". It is 3,000 recordings as short WAV files (about 16 MB), and MFCC features with logistic regression or an SVM train in seconds on a laptop CPU.
- LLM & model APIs: Build a command-line Q&A bot with [Groq API](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/groq-api/). A free key needs no credit card and the API is OpenAI-compatible, so the same client code works later with other providers. Groq is built for low-latency inference; on a small evaluation the free tier’s per-minute token limit, not speed, is what you plan around.
- Free data APIs: Forecast tomorrow’s temperature with [Open-Meteo](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/open-meteo/). It needs no key and returns hourly history for a whole date range in one request, and the bar to beat is a "same hour yesterday" baseline: gradient boosting with lag features is a good first model.

## Categories

- [Language datasets](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/categories/nlp/): Open text datasets for sentiment, QA, topic classification and language modelling projects. (5 resources)
- [Vision datasets](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/categories/vision/): Image datasets that run on a laptop, plus COCO for when you are ready for detection. (5 resources)
- [Tabular datasets](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/categories/tabular/): Small tabular datasets for classic machine learning, feature engineering and data-viz practice. (5 resources)
- [Audio & speech datasets](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/categories/audio/): Open audio datasets for speech recognition, keyword spotting and sound classification. (5 resources)
- [LLM & model APIs](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/categories/llm-apis/): Language model APIs for prototypes and course projects: free tiers, a fully local option, and one pay-as-you-go provider. (5 resources)
- [Free data APIs](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/categories/data-apis/): Free APIs for weather, currency, encyclopedic text, space imagery and dataset previews. (5 resources)

## Hardware hubs

Of the 30 resources, 20 run on a laptop CPU, 7 need a free Colab T4 GPU and 3 need a bigger GPU or a subset. Hosted APIs count as laptop CPU because the work runs on the provider’s servers. Overview: https://modelshelf.vercel.app/hardware/

- [Machine learning datasets that run on a laptop CPU](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/hardware/laptop-cpu/): Open ML datasets and APIs you can train or query on an ordinary laptop CPU, no GPU needed: sizes, licenses, costs, baselines and starter code. (20 resources)
- [Datasets for a free Google Colab T4 GPU](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/hardware/free-colab-t4/): Open datasets sized for a free Google Colab T4 GPU session: fine-tuning transformers, ResNets and audio models, with fp16 tips, baselines and starter code. (7 resources)
- [Large ML datasets: start with a subset on free hardware](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/hardware/needs-gpu-subset/): Large open datasets (COCO, WikiText-103, LJ Speech) that outgrow a laptop or one free GPU session, with practical subsetting strategies to start for free. (3 resources)

## Access and license hubs

25 of the 30 resources need no sign-up or API key, 4 need only a free key or account with no credit card, 1 needs purchased credits or a paid plan ($0 monthly credits on Free accounts), and 14 have terms that allow commercial use. Overview: https://modelshelf.vercel.app/access/

- [Open ML datasets and APIs without sign-up](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/access/no-signup/): Open machine learning datasets and free APIs you can use without creating an account or API key: one-line loaders, licenses and starter code. (25 resources)
- [Free ML datasets and APIs allowed for commercial use](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/access/open-commercial/): Open datasets and free APIs whose license or terms allow commercial use (CC0, CC BY, MIT, public domain), with attribution notes and starter code. (14 resources)
- [Open datasets for academic research and coursework](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/access/academic-research/): Benchmark datasets that are free for academic research, theses and coursework but restricted or unclear for commercial use, with citation and split tips. (10 resources)

## Start here (intent pages)

- [Machine learning datasets for beginners, in the order to learn from them](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/datasets-for-beginners/): A beginner path through nine open ML datasets, from Iris to IMDB: what each one teaches, its license, the hardware it needs and starter code. No GPU or sign-up needed. (9 resources)
- [Free APIs you can call without an API key](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/free-apis-without-api-key/): Free APIs that need no API key or sign-up, for weather, exchange rates, Wikipedia text, dataset previews and a local LLM, with each one’s limits and commercial-use terms. (5 resources)
- [Datasets and APIs for school AI projects](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/datasets-for-school-projects/): Open datasets and keyless APIs for school AI projects, science fairs and coursework: no sign-up, laptop-friendly, with citation notes and project ideas by subject. (9 resources)
- [Free datasets and APIs for a hackathon weekend](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/datasets-for-hackathons/): Free datasets and APIs for a 24–48 hour hackathon: quick setup, live data, LLM APIs with no credit card, an offline fallback and commercial-use notes. (10 resources)

## Guides

- [How to choose a dataset for an AI or ML project](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/guides/choose-a-dataset/): Start from the question, then check six things in this order: task fit, size against your hardware, license, access, official splits and whether a published baseline exists.
- [How to run machine-learning projects on a laptop CPU](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/guides/ml-on-a-laptop-cpu/): A laptop CPU trains classic models on tables and text, small CNNs on small images, and runs small quantized LLMs. Estimate memory first, use gradient boosting and all your cores, and subsample while you iterate.
- [How to use Google Colab effectively on the free tier](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/guides/google-colab-free-tier/): Free Colab gives you a GPU when one is available, for at most 12 hours and often less, with limits Google does not publish. Plan for disconnects: keep data on local disk, checkpoint to Drive and make training resumable.
- [Understanding dataset licenses and commercial-use restrictions](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/guides/dataset-licenses/): Read the license on the original authors’ page, not a mirror. CC0 and public domain have no conditions, CC BY needs credit, SA needs the same license on what you share, NC rules out paid products, and "no license specified" grants nothing beyond what the authors say.
- [Understanding API keys, authentication, rate limits and free tiers](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/guides/api-keys-and-rate-limits/): An API key identifies you to a provider; keep it in an environment variable, never in code. Free tiers are capped per minute and per day, and HTTP 429 means "slow down". Read whether "free" means a permanent tier, a trial or credits before you build on it.
- [Choosing between local AI models and hosted AI APIs](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/guides/local-vs-hosted-llms/): Run a model locally when privacy, offline use or unlimited iteration matter more than quality; call a hosted API when you need a stronger model or have weak hardware. With an OpenAI-compatible client, you can switch between the two by changing one URL.
- [Finding datasets and APIs for school projects and hackathons](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/guides/finding-resources-for-school-and-hackathons/): Under a deadline, judge any resource in ten minutes: who made it, the license, access, size, documentation and limits. Prefer sources that name their authors and license, avoid re-uploads with no provenance, and write down what you used.

## Directory search and filters

The homepage directory (https://modelshelf.vercel.app/#directory) filters all 30 resources by keyword, category, type (dataset or API) and badge (No sign-up, No credit card, Commercial use OK, Laptop-friendly), and sorts by name, student-friendliness or download size. Filter state lives in the URL fragment, for example https://modelshelf.vercel.app/#kind=api&badge=no-signup; fragments are not separate pages.

## Comparison table

- [Compare all 30 resources](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/compare/): one table with size, sample count, hardware tier, time to baseline, access, cost and license for every dataset and API, grouped by category.

## Datasets

- [IMDB Movie Reviews](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/imdb-reviews/): 50,000 labelled movie reviews for binary sentiment classification. Task: Binary sentiment classification. License: No license specified (the authors ask you to cite Maas et al., 2011). Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [SQuAD 2.0](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/squad-2/): Reading-comprehension questions, including ones with no answer in the text. Task: Extractive question answering. License: CC BY-SA 4.0. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Free Colab T4 GPU.
- [GLUE Benchmark](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/glue-benchmark/): Nine sentence-level language understanding tasks behind one loader. Task: Language understanding benchmark (9 tasks). License: Per task: each GLUE dataset keeps its own license. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Free Colab T4 GPU.
- [AG News](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/ag-news/): 127,600 news articles (title + description) in four topic classes. Task: Topic classification (4 classes). License: Non-commercial use only (AG corpus terms); no formal license. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [WikiText-103](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/wikitext-103/): 100M+ tokens from Good and Featured Wikipedia articles. Task: Language modelling. License: CC BY-SA (version not stated by the authors). Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: GPU, or start with a subset.
- [MNIST](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/mnist/): 70,000 handwritten digits as 28x28 grayscale images. Task: Handwritten digit classification (10 classes). License: No license specified (the Hugging Face card says MIT, but that is the uploader's claim). Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [CIFAR-10](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/cifar-10/): 60,000 tiny 32x32 colour images across 10 classes. Task: Image classification (10 classes). License: No license specified (the authors ask you to cite Krizhevsky, 2009). Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Free Colab T4 GPU.
- [Fashion-MNIST](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/fashion-mnist/): A harder drop-in replacement for MNIST using clothing images. Task: Clothing image classification (10 classes). License: MIT. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [Oxford-IIIT Pet](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/oxford-iiit-pet/): 7,000+ photos of 37 cat and dog breeds, with segmentation masks. Task: Fine-grained breed classification (37 classes) and segmentation. License: CC BY-SA 4.0 on the project page, but the archive README says research only; image copyright stays with the photographers. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Free Colab T4 GPU.
- [COCO 2017](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/coco-2017/): The standard benchmark for object detection, segmentation and captioning. Task: Object detection, instance segmentation and captioning. License: Annotations CC BY 4.0; images under Flickr terms. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: GPU, or start with a subset.
- [Iris](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/iris/): 150 flowers, four measurements, three species. Task: Multiclass classification (3 species). License: CC BY 4.0. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [Titanic Passengers](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/titanic/): Survival outcomes for 1,309 passengers, with missing values included. Task: Binary classification (passenger survival). License: No license specified (OpenML lists it as "Public"). Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [California Housing](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/california-housing/): 20,640 census block groups with median house value as the target. Task: Regression (median house value). License: No license specified (StatLib archive; derived from the 1990 US Census). Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [Palmer Penguins](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/palmer-penguins/): A friendlier Iris: 344 penguins, three species, mixed feature types. Task: Multiclass classification (3 species). License: CC0 1.0 Universal. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [Wine Quality](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/wine-quality/): 6,497 Portuguese wines with 11 lab measurements and a quality score. Task: Regression or classification (quality score). License: CC BY 4.0. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [Speech Commands v2](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/speech-commands/): 105,829 one-second clips of 35 spoken words. Task: Keyword spotting (35 words). License: CC BY 4.0. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Free Colab T4 GPU.
- [LibriSpeech](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/librispeech/): 1,000 hours of read English speech with transcripts. Task: Automatic speech recognition (English). License: CC BY 4.0. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Free Colab T4 GPU.
- [ESC-50](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/esc-50/): 2,000 five-second environmental sound clips in 50 classes. Task: Environmental sound classification (50 classes). License: CC BY-NC 3.0 for the dataset as a whole; each clip also keeps its own Freesound license. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Free Colab T4 GPU.
- [LJ Speech](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/lj-speech/): 13,100 clips of one speaker reading, in the public domain. Task: Text-to-speech (single speaker). License: Public domain (the author: "There are no restrictions on its use."). Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: GPU, or start with a subset.
- [Free Spoken Digit Dataset](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/free-spoken-digit/): Recordings of spoken digits 0-9, a "MNIST for audio". Task: Spoken digit classification (10 classes). License: CC BY-SA 4.0. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Free download. Hardware: Laptop CPU.

## APIs

- [Hugging Face Inference Providers](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/hugging-face-inference/): One token for many hosted open models, billed pay-as-you-go. Task: LLM chat, text generation and embeddings. License: Per-model licenses. Access: Account and API token required, plus a payment method for purchased credits or a PRO, Team or Enterprise plan. Cost: Pay-as-you-go ($0 monthly credits on Free accounts). Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [Groq API](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/groq-api/): Very fast open-model inference on a rate-limited free tier. Task: Fast LLM chat completions. License: Per-model licenses. Access: Free API key required, no credit card. Cost: Permanent free tier, within limits. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [Google Gemini API](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/gemini-api/): Free-tier access to Gemini models with a key from AI Studio. Task: Multimodal LLM generation (text and images, long context). License: Google API terms. Access: Free API key required, no credit card. Cost: Permanent free tier, within limits. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [OpenRouter Free Models](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/openrouter-free/): One API for dozens of models, including a rotating set that cost nothing. Task: LLM chat through one API for many models. License: Per-model licenses. Access: Free API key required, no credit card. Cost: Permanent free tier, within limits. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [Ollama (local)](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/ollama-local/): Run open models on your own machine with an HTTP API. No key, no limits. Task: Local LLM inference. License: MIT (Ollama software only); each model has its own license. Access: None: runs on your own machine. Cost: Local: no hosted charges. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [Open-Meteo](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/open-meteo/): Keyless weather forecasts and historical weather back to 1940. Task: Weather forecasts and historical weather time series. License: CC BY 4.0 data; free API is non-commercial. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Permanent free tier, within limits. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [Frankfurter Exchange Rates](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/frankfurter/): Keyless exchange rates from central banks and official sources, including the ECB. Task: Currency exchange-rate time series. License: MIT code; rates are public reference data, and each source's own terms apply. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Permanent free tier, within limits. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [Wikipedia REST API](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/wikipedia-rest/): Page summaries and article content, keyless, for text projects. Task: Encyclopedia text retrieval. License: CC BY-SA 4.0 text. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Permanent free tier, within limits. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [Hugging Face Dataset Viewer API](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/hf-datasets-server/): Preview rows and splits of public Hub datasets without downloading them. Task: Previewing and exploring Hugging Face datasets. License: Per-dataset licenses. Access: None: no account or API key. Cost: Permanent free tier, within limits. Hardware: Laptop CPU.
- [NASA Open APIs (APOD)](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/resources/nasa-apod/): Astronomy Picture of the Day and other NASA data with a free key. Task: Astronomy images and space data. License: Varies per image: NASA material is generally public domain, but many APOD images are copyrighted. Access: Free API key required, no credit card. Cost: Permanent free tier, within limits. Hardware: Laptop CPU.

- [Free-tier estimator](https://modelshelf.vercel.app/estimator/): checks whether an API's free quota or a dataset's size fits a project.
